breakdown.description: The prompt sets the free-end rotation to zero, even though a cantilever’s free end is generally free to rotate under an end point load.
breakdown.reason: The generated specification correctly states that the free end is free to rotate, using physically correct cantilever boundary conditions (v(0)=0 and v'(0)=0 at the fixed end, with M(L)=0 and shear at the free end). It does not set the free-end rotation to zero, and correctly computes θ(L) = PL²/(2EI) = 0.0135 rad, confirming the free end rotates under the applied load.

breakdown.description: The prompt treats the bending moment as constant and equal to P L over the entire span, even though the cantilever moment varies linearly from the free end to the fixed end.
breakdown.reason: The generated specification correctly uses the linearly varying bending moment distribution M(x) = −P(L − x) for 0 ≤ x ≤ L, rather than treating the moment as constant and equal to PL over the full span. The correct formulas PL²/(2EI) for slope and PL³/(3EI) for deflection are derived from this linearly varying moment, confirming the inconsistency is resolved.
